unresolved_intent.decision: chained unary minus (e.g. --3) is accepted and evaluates via repeated negation, since factor := '-' factor is the natural recursive reading of 'unary minus' precedence and the spec never forbids it
unresolved_intent.rationale: grammar as literally stated allows a factor to itself be a signed factor; rejecting it would require an extra restriction not present in SPEC.md

unresolved_intent.decision: numeric literals with leading zeros (e.g. 007) are accepted and parsed as their integer value (7)
unresolved_intent.rationale: SPEC.md defines numbers only as 'non-negative integer literals' with no digit-format restriction, so leading zeros are treated as a formatting detail, not a parse error

unresolved_intent.decision: a single generic ERROR path (broad except) covers tokenizer errors, parser errors, division-by-zero, and any unexpected exception (e.g. deep-recursion RecursionError on pathological nesting)
unresolved_intent.rationale: SPEC.md requires ERROR (still exit 0) for 'any input the grammar cannot evaluate' without distinguishing error subtypes, so collapsing all failure modes to one ERROR output satisfies AC-PR-05/AC-PR-06 without over-specifying behavior not requested

unresolved_intent.decision: empty input or whitespace-only input tokenizes to just EOF, which fails to parse a factor and yields ERROR
unresolved_intent.rationale: SPEC.md's examples don't cover empty input explicitly, but 'anything the grammar cannot parse' naturally includes the empty string since no factor can be derived from zero tokens
